title: Semantic fragmentation recovery and toolcall idempotency shim
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Clients reconnecting to SSE streams can receive partial JSON fragments that cross semantic boundaries (e.g., mid-toolcall, mid-structured-output). Current resume tokens are byte-offset driven and do not guarantee that the next resumed message will preserve tool/function call atomicity or structured-object invariants. That causes duplicate tool invocations, malformed structured outputs, and makes compatibility with older SDKs difficult.

Goal: Implement a compatibility-focused shim and server-side protocol support that enables: (1) semantic fragment anchors that mark safe resume boundaries, (2) ephemeral resume checkpoints that can be negotiated on reconnect, and (3) toolcall idempotency enforcement across resume events. The solution must be backward compatible with existing clients that only understand legacy resume tokens and must provide a graceful degradation path (best-effort semantic resume when anchors are unavailable).
acceptance_criteria: Server emits semantic anchors in the stream (anchor events) for every completed top-level output unit (message, toolcall, structured object) and documents format in protocol guide.
Resume token format extended to optionally include anchor ids and ephemeral checkpoint ids while preserving legacy token parsing for older clients.
On reconnect the server can return the next complete semantic unit to the client; partial fragments are never forwarded to clients unless client explicitly requests partial-mode.
Toolcall idempotency: server deduplicates duplicate tool invocation requests within a configurable dedup window (default 30s) when a duplicate toolcall id is observed across reconnects.

Compatibility shim available in runtime to translate legacy offset tokens to nearest semantic anchor when possible; if translation unavailable server falls back to best-effort prefix reassembly and annotates response with fallback-warning.
E2E tests cover normal stream, mid-toolcall disconnect, duplicate reconnect that would have caused double-invoke (now deduped), and legacy-client resume behavior.
Design reviewed and approved by API and Security; migration plan exists and default behavior does not break existing customers.
Console telemetry exposes anchor hit/miss rates and dedup incidence with a dashboard under streaming-protocols.
Performance regression <5% p99 latency increase for resumed connections compared to current resume baseline (measured in workload harness).
